newsitem.title: JAPAN: Scandal-hit DKB suffers hefty deposit withdrawals.
newsitem.headline: Scandal-hit DKB suffers hefty deposit withdrawals.

text.p: Scandal-tainted Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd said on Thursday it was hit by heavy deposit withdrawals last month as individual customers pulled out some 150 billion yen from their accounts.

A spokesman for the commercial bank told Reuters that the amount of individual deposits slid by nearly 150 billion yen in May alone, but said he could not confirm whether the move was continuing in June.
"We do not publicise our amount of deposits on a monthly basis, but nearly 150 billion yen worth of individual deposits appear to have been withdrawn in May," he said.
Individual deposits at DKB totalled 12.7 trillion yen at end-March 1996, the latest fiscal year for which figures are available.

In the Tokyo money market, DKB has been active in raising funds, which has helped push up short-term interest rates, traders say. The action is widely viewed as a pre-emptive measure to secure sufficient funds, in part to meet further withdrawals.
There were even rumours in the market earlier this week, later denied by the central bank, that DKB may be suspended from taking part in the Bank of Japan's market operations.

The DKB spokesman said the bank was taking more than its usual amount of funds from the market in order to cope with possible further deposit withdrawals. "We are raising more funds than usual from the market, taking into consideration our possible future fund needs," the spokesman said.
Asked about the impact of the scandal on the bank's business, the spokesman said, "(The scandal) has not shaken our business. We have no financing problems."

On Tuesday, four former DKB executives were arrested on suspicion of violating the Commercial Code with payoffs in the form of illicit loans to a "sokaiya" racketeer. The arrest came shortly after the bank unveiled a top management shake-up, its second in less than a month.

The latest arrests followed the arrests last Thursday of four other DKB officials on suspicion of extending uncollateralised loans to Ryuichi Koike, the racketeer at the centre of a scandal which has also embroiled Nomura Securities Co Ltd. -- Tokyo Equities Desk, +81-3-3432-9404
